discipline: Knowledge representation and information design: what a law asserts (which condition, given what, on which model) and what a drawing of it commits the reader to. AI-written. Read-only work: I read places-v1.json, all 88 decisions with their notes, the atlas's dynamics.json (families A in full, H and E in part), premises.json, situations.json, draw.py and layout.json, and the Lean statements of uniform_locks, turned_by_loss, Thinned.kept_iff, locked_along, window_never_read, deadline, borne_by_shapers_favours_iff and shapers_left. The classification of the 88 below is one reader's pass, not put to a refuter; counts could move by a few.
verdict_on_present:
What it gets right: (1) plain names a stranger understands, with an example each; (2) every mark traced to a Lean statement and refuted by a second reader, with 'no arrow' allowed as an answer (50 of 88 items were refused an arrow, which is the map's honesty); (3) it already found that places overlap; (4) as a first picture of one loop it is the only thing a person has looked at and said yes to. That last point is evidence no design argument outranks.

Where it is dominated: as a STORE. The same data plus three fields (the question a place answers; the logical shape of a law; the model a law is proved on) can redraw today's picture unchanged and also shows what today's hides. So the present structure is strictly dominated as a data structure, and not dominated as a five-minute picture of one loop.

The core defect is one primitive doing five jobs. 'Arrow between two places' fits a minority of what the laws say: of 88 items, 38 are arrows; 9 of those are two-way iffs that say where a line lies, not that anything crosses it; 8 are single built examples; 3 are readings. That leaves 18 of 88 that are one-way changes backed by a general law. Atlas-wide it will be worse: 57 of 103 transitions are thresholds in a parameter, 31 are time bounds, 160 of 321 exits are witnesses, 29 are 'leaving needs' laws.
dominated_where: One law drawn as two arrows from two different tails: ClosedCapture.turned_by_loss is closed-capture exit 1 (judged-inside -> cost-counts) and a-counter-rule-read-from-its-own-share exit 2 (holds-itself -> cost-counts). The tail differs only because judged-inside IS holds-itself plus two other answers. 8 of the 83 distinct laws are cited by more than one item.

One iff drawn as two unrelated arrows: ClosedCapture.Thinned.kept_iff is readers-drawn-from-the-selected exit 1 (felt -> cost-counts) and transition 2 (felt -> past-turning-back). The Lean is a single fork: held for good exactly when those not ahead are no more than those ahead at that re-setting. The picture loses that the two outcomes are exhaustive, and sends the second into a place about TIME though the statement has no time in it. 'Past turning back' pools 'too late' (ReadInTime.deadline, Web.too_late_of_alike) with 'outnumbered' (kept_iff, kept_past_least).

One fork split across two tails: ReadInTime.turned_early_iff is drawn from holds-itself (shaping-read-by-readers-drawn exit 1) and its other branch kept_early_iff from felt (loss-read-in-time-by-the-others transition 1).

The firmest-looking edge is not a change: draw.py styles each pair by its best law, so uncounted <-> felt is drawn exact and two-headed on Web.separates_all_iff_member, Web.readOffCouplings_alike_iff and Web.readableInTime_iff, which say when a loss reaches someone with a say. The only items showing a noticer actually coming to have a say are two built examples (Clearing.pool_closes_gap, PoolCourse.scheduled_apart).

A wildcard cannot be a tail: RuleCapture.uniform_locks says ANY start is held after the second rebuilding where the rule favours one side at every lead. A place is a point, so the item became 'inside holds-itself', and the map reports that no law leads into the hold (in-degree 0). Three readers drew three different arrows for it, as they did for locked_along, shapers_left and recoverable_iff_regime: each time the item was not an arrow.

Paths the eye composes that no law supports: 63 of the 79 two-step paths join laws from Lean modules that share no namespace (some of those modules are built on one another, so the true count is lower). The spine uncounted -> felt (Web) -> cost-counts (ClosedCapture, ReadInTime) crosses a join the atlas itself records as a reading (compose reading-a-loss-in-time -> loss-read-in-time-by-the-others). holds-itself -> all-on-one (DrawnReplacement.lost_ge) -> several-ways (SharedCodes.run_kept_iff) joins a count of rule-benders to a shared word with no bridge at all. Of the atlas's 10 compose entries, 6 are proved.

The list names troubles: six places are one answer of a question whose other answer has no place (still time; noticers still there; goes on; judged by others; checkers picked by others; the pattern ends with its members), and 'rule rebuilt from its own results' has no place though three tests assume it. cost-counts has 8 arrows in and none out, past-turning-back 5 in and none out, uncounted 12 out and none in. This is the structural source of the dualism the director hears, and denying it in prose does not remove it.

Free-text tests and conditions cannot be matched to a real case or to each other: several arrow conditions restate the destination's definition (closed-capture exit 1: 'the rule comes to register what is used up' -> 'The cost counts'), so the condition carries no information the arrowhead does not.
Scaling: adding 346 items to a flat list gives 35 to 40 boxes whose honest decisions are mostly 'inside' and 'stays'. Family A read by the present method would be nearly edgeless.
false_premise:
Three, in the question and in the hypothesis.

1. 'Pareto frontier' assumes one structure whose counts can all be maximised. They trade: the five-minute picture must leave out most seams and thresholds; the faithful store must keep them. The answer is a dominated/not-dominated check per job, and the result is split: the flat list is dominated as a store, the node-link picture of one loop is not dominated as a first view.

2. That the data structure is the binding limit. It is not. The laws live on about 108 Lean modules (only 18 appear in more than one family) joined by 10 bridges, 6 proved. No structure can draw a more connected map than that truthfully. The best a structure can do is make the joins themselves visible, which also tells the work which bridges to prove next.

3. In the hypothesis: 'a real case is a tuple of answers'. No law is proved on a model that has all the aspects, so a full tuple invites reading laws jointly that were never joined. A real case is a web (situations.json already has the schema), and most answers read off it are 'not known'. Also: whether any of this is optimal for human understanding cannot be settled by design or by AI readers (that was the loop that scored 8). One person, one case they know, ten minutes with the question sheet: can they place it and say what can happen next.
proposal_in_one_paragraph: Test of the hypothesis on all 88. As stated in (b), a law is (aspect, from, to, given answers): 13 fit (10 changes, 3 keepings), 19 with plain staying laws. 13 more move one aspect but their gate is a quantity of the law's own model (who outnumbers whom at which round, a bound on rounds, who hears whom). 9 are not changes at all but lines between two answers in a parameter (all drawn as arrows today); 11 sit inside one answer (which side of a tipping count, how fast); 8 need an aspect the hypothesis lacks; 2 are misnamed (PairSelection's giving in pairs drawn as 'bending the rule pays'); 9 with a law stay unplaced (2 are bridges between models, 5 are caught by the missing aspects); 15 have no law. What survives: (a) as an INDEX, since 11 of 15 places are already one answer to one question and overlap becomes ordinary; but not seven global aspects (this region needs 9 to 11, family A shares 2 or 3 and needs about 5 of its own) and not as a state space of tuples. (b) fails as the one shape; it survives as three shapes with the gate split into answers and a measure, and its computed loops survive only with seams counted. (c) survives as what a question IS (the state of one relation among a fixed cast, which is the situations.json schema) and as a small picture per answer; it fails as 'a change is a relation appearing or ending', since about two thirds of the laws compare amounts or times. (d) survives. What I would build: keep the places and their plain names; make each place an answer to a named question about one relation; make the unit of the store the LAW, one card per Lean law, with shape keeps / moves / line, the atlas's own strength, a gate (answers on other questions plus the model's own measure in plain words), and the model it is proved on; record seams between models as first-class; and store a real case as the web it already is, with answers read off it and 'not known' allowed.
schema:
Five record kinds.

question: id; ask (en, zh), a question anyone can put to a situation; about (one relation among the cast: who or what, relation, whom or what, e.g. 'the loss, reaches, those with a say'); neighbourhood (which part of the cast, so families group without a new vocabulary); answers (2 to 4, mutually exclusive, in a natural order where there is one).

answer (this is a PLACE): id; say (the plain label, en and zh); example; pattern (the relations that hold, as cast triples with present / absent / late / more than, replacing the free-text test); aka (the field's known names); how_far (law, reading, open). Answers of one question exclude each other; answers of different questions can hold together, so 'judged only from inside' is a named combination of four answers and has no record of its own.

card (this is a CHANGE, and also a staying and a threshold): law (Lean name; one card per law, the atlas items that cite it listed in items); shape, one of keeps (the answer stays while the gate holds), moves (the answer changes), line (where the border between two answers lies in the model's own quantity, no change in time); of (the question); from (an answer, or 'any'); to (an answer, or for an exact law the branches, each with its condition); given (list of question-answer pairs on OTHER questions); measure (one plain sentence for what the model compares when the gate is a quantity, kept as text); strength (the atlas's words unchanged: exact, sufficient, necessary, witness, reading, open); on (the Lean module and base it is proved on); drops (the atlas premise id).

seam: answer; between (two modules); how, one of proved (the compose law named), built-on (one module's definitions used by the other, e.g. shared premise ruleshaping-pos), read, none; source. Any two cards chained through an answer either share a module or cross a seam, and the seam is shown.

case (a REAL CASE): the situations.json entry as it is (formations, conditions, couplings, readers, rule, time, who bears) plus answers: for each question an answer or 'not known', with the couplings or readers that show it. Derived, never stored: the cards whose gate the case meets (what can happen next), the questions it cannot answer and the cards with no law (what is missing), the seams those cards cross.
drawn_from_it:
Two drawings and one text, all generated from the same records.

1. The board, in lanes. One horizontal lane per question, its answers as boxes left to right in their order; lanes grouped by neighbourhood. A moves card is an arrow along its lane, from answer to answer, tail on the lane's left margin when from is 'any'. Its gate is a thin tie from the arrow up or down to each answer in given on other lanes, shown on hover or at the deepest level. An exact card with branches is drawn as one fork with its measure written once at the split. A keeps card is a loop mark on the answer, tied to its gate. A line card is a tick on the border between two boxes, never an arrowhead. A witness is a dot on the path, not a line style. A card with no law is dashed. Where two cards chained through a box are on different modules, a stitch mark on that box, filled if the seam is proved, hollow if read, a gap if none. Empty stretches of a lane stay visibly empty. Three levels of the same drawing: one loop (only the cards of one cycle of gates, about six, which may be shown as today's node-link picture since for one loop the two coincide); a region (its 8 to 11 lanes); the whole atlas (neighbourhoods folded to one lane each). A case is one highlighted box per lane, or a question mark, with the cards it meets lit. Needs no hand layout beyond the order of lanes.

2. The page per answer, about 150 words, generated: the label; a small picture of its pattern in the cast (4 to 6 nodes, only those the law's model has); 'found with' (answers it holds together with in some law); then four short lists straight from the cards: what keeps it, what moves out and in, what leaving needs, shown once (witnesses), and 'no law shows'. Known names at the foot.

The text: the question sheet for a real case, which is the lanes read top to bottom, each answer followed by the cards it opens. It extends the four and five questions USES.md already offers.
worked_sample:
QUESTIONS AND PLACES (9 of the 15 places, as answers).
- Where does the rule come from? set from outside [fixed-rule] | rebuilt from its own results [no place today; hidden in three tests].
- What has it settled on? several ways [several-ways] | one side held [holds-itself, without the 'rebuilt' clause] | everyone on one [all-on-one].
- How far does the loss reach? no one with a say [uncounted] | someone with a say [felt] | into the rule [cost-counts].
- Are those who would notice still there? there [no place today] | removed [noticers-gone].
- Is there still time? still time [no place today] | past turning back [past-turning-back].
- Does a costly practice pay its doers? costs [shaping-costs] | pays [shaping-pays].
- judged-inside = rebuilt + those ahead judge + one side held + no one with a say: a combination, drawn as four lit boxes.

CARDS (12 cards for 17 of the items; number in brackets is the row in decisions.json).
1. ClosedCapture.turned_by_loss. Items: closed-capture exit 1 [2], a-counter-rule-read-from-its-own-share exit 2 [30]. moves; of settled; from one side held; to not held for that side; given reach = into the rule (the rule stops favouring past a limit of loss); sufficient; on ClosedCapture; drops closedcapture-unread. Today: two arrows from two tails.
2. ClosedCapture.Thinned.kept_iff. Items: readers-drawn-from-the-selected exit 1 [5], transition 2 [7]. moves, exact, a fork; of settled; from one side held; given reach = someone with a say, at a re-setting with the loss past its bound; measure: are those not ahead more than those ahead then; branches: no -> held for good, yes -> not held. Today: two arrows, one into a place about time.
3. ReadInTime.turned_iff, kept_early_iff, turned_early_iff. Items: loss-read-in-time-by-the-others exit 1 [20], transition 1 [21]; shaping-read-by-readers-drawn-from-the-selected exit 1 [14]. One fork of settled; given reach = someone with a say from round N; measure: judgments pooled, loss included, at N and the next round. Today: three arrows from two tails.
4. ReadInTime.deadline. Item: loss-read-in-time-by-the-others transition 2 [22]. moves; of time; still time -> past; given settled = one side held with those ahead favoured strictly at the start; measure: a bound on rounds from the starting numbers (a bound, not the moment); sufficient.
5. RuleCapture.uniform_locks. Item: capture-through-the-rule transition 1 [1]. moves; of settled; from ANY; to one side held, within two rebuildings; given source = rebuilt; measure: the rule favours the same side at every lead; sufficient. Today: 'inside', so the hold has no way in.
6. PoolFromCourse.locked_along. Item: the-lock-draws-its-readers-out exit 1 [39]. keeps; of settled = one side held; necessary: leaving needs a remaking that differs from what the lead alone gives (reach other than 'no one'), or the lead to shrink.
7. PoolFromCourse.window_never_read. Item: same dynamic, transition 1 [42]. keeps; settled = one side held, for good, while the loss passes every bound; given there = removed before they register it; sufficient.
8. Web.readableInTime_iff. Item: reading-a-loss-in-time transition 1 [56]. line; between reach = no one and reach = someone with a say; measure: the first moment anyone with a say can tell comes before the point of no return; exact; on Web. Today: an arrow.
9. Web.too_late_of_alike, too_late_of_own. Items: reading-a-loss-in-time exits 1, 2 [52, 53]. moves; of time; still time -> past; given reach = no one with a say can tell until then; sufficient; on Web.
10. SharedCodes.agrees_every_start_iff and run_kept_iff. Items: a-code-formed-between-formations exits 1, 2 [31, 32]. moves; of settled; any -> everyone on one exactly where the hearings trace everyone to one source; everyone on one -> several ways when a member takes a way heard from outside. on SharedCodes, which has no rule, loss or noticers: the other lanes are 'not asked' there.
11. RuleShaping.favours_iff [9] and PairSelection.assorted_favours_iff [43] (shaping-the-rule transition 1; offspring-read-from-giving-that-waits transition 1). line; of pays; measure: what comes back to the doers alone against the cost. [43] is on PairSelection, about giving in pairs.
12. PoolFromCourse.borne_by_shapers_favours_iff with the witness Borne.shapers_left. Item: the-lock-draws-its-readers-out exit 3 [41], today 'leads-out, no listed place', three readers three arrows. line; of pays; given a question the list lacks, 'does the loss fall back on those ahead' = yes; measure: cost plus loss against return (c + l <= s). Witness: held at steps 1 to 3, left at step 4, nobody having noticed.

SEAMS.
- reach = someone with a say: Web (card 8) against ClosedCapture and ReadInTime (cards 2, 3): read (compose reading-a-loss-in-time -> loss-read-in-time-by-the-others, standing reading).
- settled = everyone on one: SharedCodes [31-36], CountedCodes [37, 38], DrawnReplacement [15], SelectionTerm [58], Flow [68]: none. Five different things under one name.
- pays: RuleShaping against PairSelection: proved (assorted_counts, window_echo_shaped; these are offspring compose 1 and 2 [46, 47], 'unresolved' today, and here they have a home). RuleShaping against DrawnShaping and ReadInTime: built-on.
what_it_reveals:
1. The loop, which the flat map cannot show. A hold is not a path back into a box; it is conditions gating one another. From the cards: the hold sets in from any start (card 5); leaving it needs the loss to reach someone whose judgment remakes the rule (card 6, necessary); the loss reaches no one once those who would notice are removed before they register it (card 7, sufficient); they are removed where what is used up is what they stand on (ReadingsSpread.Commons.cleared_spreads [61], a witness; [81] and [83], readings; inside PoolFromCourse it is the premise K <= N, not a theorem); and it is used up because the rule does better by it (Flow.keeping_optimum_takes_slack [84], another model, seam read). A cycle of four gates: two proved on one model, one a premise and a witness, one across a read seam. On the flat map holds-itself has in-degree 0 and there is no cycle through it at all. This is how far the loop of the meta-attractor's shape has been seen in this region, on one picture.

2. Holes, as empty lanes. No card moves 'where the rule comes from' or 'who judges it' (fixed-rule 0 in 0 out; judged-inside 0 in; checkers-inside no law). Every way from 'no one with a say' to 'someone' is either a line saying when it is so ([56], [70], [75]) or a built example in which the noticer is put in from outside ([71] the pool includes them, [72] a fixed date); [76] and [82] say nothing inside secures one. So the two lanes an alignment design would act on are exactly the ones no law moves.

3. A dependency. Card 12 ties 'does the loss fall back on those ahead' to 'does it pay' by an exact line. The hinge the ethics rests on (where relations close, a course's costs lie within what affects its own going on) appears inside the capture region as a threshold; today it is a 'leads-out'.

4. What 'leads-out' and 'unresolved' mean. About 17 of the 88 items are gated by a question whose home is another family: falls back / made good ([41], [62], [67], [73], [74]); goes on and drawn below need ([48], [59], [62], [87]); chance ([15], [18]); what a shared way can tell apart ([34], [35]); giving in pairs ([43] to [47]); the margin ([54]). Families join through shared questions, not through arrows.

5. Asymmetry. 'Into the rule' and 'past turning back' have laws in and none out. The board shows this as a lane with arrows one way; whether it is absorbing or merely unstudied is then a visible open item, not a property of a 'bad place'.
loses_or_risks:
- More names, not fewer. Making the unlisted answers explicit turns 15 places into about 9 questions with about 22 answers in this region; the whole atlas is nearer 20 to 25 questions and 60 answers than the hypothesised 7 by 4. Each page gets shorter; the vocabulary does not shrink.
- A lane board reads less like a map than boxes and arrows. The director said yes to the latter. Keep it as the first view of one loop; if the board is shown first it may read as a control panel.
- Two-answer questions can bring the dualism back as pairs of opposites. Mitigation is structural only in part: both directions drawn side by side, names by what happens. It still needs an eye.
- A lit box on every lane tempts a reader to apply all the cards jointly. Stitches say otherwise, and stitches are easy to ignore.
- The gate of each card (which answers on which other questions) is a curated reading, not checked by Lean. A wrong gate makes a computed loop wrong. Every computed loop should carry its weakest strength and its seam count, and none should be called proved unless all its cards are on one module or its seams are.
- The measure stays free text for about 33 of the 73 law-bearing items here (model quantities, lines, tipping counts). Those are not computable and will not become so.
- 'Module' is a coarse stand-in for 'model': some modules share definitions, some hold several models. Seams derived by script will over- and under-report until read.
- The cast pictures can suggest more than a law's model contains (the capture laws on any type have a share and a rule, no people). Draw only what the model has.
- My count of how often a change is 'a relation appearing or ending' (about one third) was estimated, not classified item by item.
cost_to_build:
By script, from what exists: one card per law with its items merged (83 laws for 88 items here); strength, drops and base from dynamics.json; the module from the law's name; a first guess at shape from strength and the transition kind (exact threshold, tipping in a parameter, critical mass -> line; window or deadline, pace bound -> a time bound; witness -> shown once; 'stays' and 'inside' decisions -> keeps or line); seams from the 10 compose entries with their standing, from premise ids shared between modules in premises.json (ruleshaping-pos already lists RuleShaping, DrawnShaping, DrawnReplacement and ReadInTime laws), and from Lean imports; 'found with'; the board, the pages and the question sheet; for a case, the matching cards. The premise ledger itself is not a factoring and should not be used as one: 1,652 distinct premises are taken across 183 dynamics and almost all by one dynamic.

By reading: the question each place answers (15 places here, an hour; about 60 answers atlas-wide); the relation each question is about (20 to 25); for each card the split of today's condition_en into given and measure and the check of shape (73 here, roughly 350 more; it rides on the settle-and-refute pass already run per item, one more field, perhaps a third more work, and fewer reader splits since items that are not arrows now have a home); a small pattern per answer; the answers of each real case.

Not buildable from data: the seams themselves. 'Read' and 'none' become 'proved' only by new Lean.
scales_to_other_families:
Family A (29 dynamics, 40 exits, 30 transitions), read in full; H and E in part.

The seven hypothesised aspects do not carry. A has no judge, no count, no noticers with a say, no bending that pays. Two carry and are central there: the point of no return (margin-of-a-regime, threshold-in-the-state-plane, a-cascade-along-total-dependence: 15 items, where region one only borrows it) and where the rule or reader comes from (a-rule-with-no-holder-does-not-return: taught from outside against taught by members; a-reader-rebuilt-from-its-stock-ends-with-it: rebuilt from the supply against from the level). 'Goes on or ended' and 'by rule or by chance' (exit-from-a-margin, fixation-by-drift), both missing from the hypothesis, are A's own. A needs about five more: draw within or beyond what renews; level above or below the point; dependence fixed or able to switch (three-outcomes-of-a-loss); a reserve; what feeds it and what it is part of. So a fixed tuple per situation is an illusion; a new set per family is also wrong. What holds is that the questions each region lacked are another family's centre, so the families join through questions.

The record kinds hold without change, and fit A better than arrows do. A's 30 transitions are 11 time bounds, 10 lines (exact threshold, tipping, joint threshold), 3 by chance, 4 routes that are readings; its 40 exits are 20 witnesses and 9 'leaving needs' laws. Under the present method A would be boxes with almost no arrows. As cards: RegimeMargin.ends_iff_below is a line on 'level against the point' with measure 'starts below H + y'; Web.Carries.ends_within is a time bound gated by reserve; Flow.fed_beyond_level_at is a necessary keeps.

Two cross-family joins the structure proposes and no law yet gives (candidates, to be marked as readings): region one's open place 'the pattern outlives its members' against H's a-pattern-lasts-through-passing (Web.ByPassing.ends_within: with no carrier passing it on, nothing carries it after d steps); and region one's 'ended' ([87], Web.optimum_broken_iff_capacity) against A's ending laws on the dependant.

E's laws are all 'tipping in a parameter' (5 of 5): lines on one question, 'does giving come back', with a proved seam into 'does it pay'. Where it may strain: F (cycles are a property of a course, likely a fourth answer to 'what has it settled on': a rest, one side, a cycle) and G (59 exits, 36 witnesses, no transitions: mostly 'shown once' dots, which will look thin and should).
first_change: Give each of the 15 places the question it answers, add the unlisted answers as empty boxes, and re-lay the existing map with one row per question. It needs one field in places-v1.json and new positions in layout.json; draw.py and the 88 decisions are untouched. It is an hour's work and shows at once which of the 38 arrows run along a lane and which cross lanes (the crossing ones are those that hide a gate and a consequence in one stroke), puts every answer beside its other answer with no ranking, turns the lanes into the question sheet for a real case, and makes the other families' places come out as answers to questions and not as a longer list of troubles. Because the remaining families are being proposed now, the second change should be settled before their 346 items are adjudicated: replace the decision kinds arrow / stays / inside / leads-out / unresolved with shape (keeps, moves, line), given, measure and the module, since re-deciding 346 items later is the expensive mistake.
